blocks.html: In distributed systems:
blocks.text: In distributed systems:

blocks.html: Data is distributed across multiple nodes.
blocks.text: Data is distributed across multiple nodes.

blocks.html: Nodes need to communicate with each other for the application to function correctly.
blocks.text: Nodes need to communicate with each other for the application to function correctly.

blocks.html: But
blocks.text: But

blocks.html: Machines can crash.
blocks.text: Machines can crash.

blocks.html: Network links between nodes can fail.
blocks.text: Network links between nodes can fail.

blocks.html: And when such things happen
blocks.text: And when such things happen

blocks.html: Either, the application services can be halted, making it unavailable to users.
blocks.text: Either, the application services can be halted, making it unavailable to users.

blocks.html: Or, the application can continue operating, but with certain trade-offs.
blocks.text: Or, the application can continue operating, but with certain trade-offs.

blocks.html: These trade-offs in distributed system design are explained by the CAP Theorem.
blocks.text: These trade-offs in distributed system design are explained by the CAP Theorem.

blocks.html: [C]: Consistency
blocks.text: [C]: Consistency

blocks.html: Every read reflects the most recent completed write (or returns an error).
blocks.text: Every read reflects the most recent completed write (or returns an error).

blocks.html: Strong Consistency (Linearizability)
blocks.text: Strong Consistency (Linearizability)

blocks.html: A write is considered successful only when it is durable and visible to all future reads.
blocks.text: A write is considered successful only when it is durable and visible to all future reads.

blocks.html: Any client, reading from any node, will always see the latest committed value — never stale data.
blocks.text: Any client, reading from any node, will always see the latest committed value — never stale data.

blocks.html: From the client’s perspective, the system behaves like there is a single, up-to-date copy of the data.
blocks.text: From the client’s perspective, the system behaves like there is a single, up-to-date copy of the data.

blocks.html: Consistency is used in many contexts with different meanings. Consistency: Definitions Based on Context provides an overview of these different definitions.
blocks.text: Consistency is used in many contexts with different meanings. Consistency: Definitions Based on Context provides an overview of these different definitions.

blocks.html: [A]: Availability
blocks.text: [A]: Availability

blocks.html: Every request receives a response — which need not to be correct.
blocks.text: Every request receives a response — which need not to be correct.

blocks.html: The system remains responsive at all times.
blocks.text: The system remains responsive at all times.

blocks.html: Even if some nodes are slow or down, other nodes must still reply.
blocks.text: Even if some nodes are slow or down, other nodes must still reply.

blocks.html: Clients never get stuck waiting indefinitely; they always get some answer.
blocks.text: Clients never get stuck waiting indefinitely; they always get some answer.

blocks.html: [P]: Partition Tolerance
blocks.text: [P]: Partition Tolerance

blocks.html: The system continues to operate even if communication between nodes is lost.
blocks.text: The system continues to operate even if communication between nodes is lost.

blocks.html: Network failures may split the system into groups of nodes that can’t talk to each other (a partition).
blocks.text: Network failures may split the system into groups of nodes that can’t talk to each other (a partition).

blocks.html: Despite this, the system must keep functioning, not shut down.
blocks.text: Despite this, the system must keep functioning, not shut down.

blocks.html: Design must tolerate unreliable networks where partitions are inevitable.
blocks.text: Design must tolerate unreliable networks where partitions are inevitable.

blocks.html: Partition Tolerance is also referred as Fault Tolerance.
blocks.text: Partition Tolerance is also referred as Fault Tolerance.

blocks.html: Example: Consistency, Availability and Partition Tolerance
blocks.text: Example: Consistency, Availability and Partition Tolerance

blocks.html: Let us say we have three nodes, all up, and can communicate to each other.
blocks.text: Let us say we have three nodes, all up, and can communicate to each other.

blocks.html: A client writes an update to node B.
blocks.text: A client writes an update to node B.

blocks.html: The update is replicated to A and C for the operation to be considered successful.
blocks.text: The update is replicated to A and C for the operation to be considered successful.

blocks.html: A subsequent read from any node (A, B, or C) will always return the latest value.
blocks.text: A subsequent read from any node (A, B, or C) will always return the latest value.

blocks.html: This is consistency.
blocks.text: This is consistency.

blocks.html: Now, Node B goes down due to a hardware failure.
blocks.text: Now, Node B goes down due to a hardware failure.

blocks.html: But, Nodes A and C are still active and can serve the client requests.
blocks.text: But, Nodes A and C are still active and can serve the client requests.

blocks.html: The system remains available because clients can still interact with A and C.
blocks.text: The system remains available because clients can still interact with A and C.

blocks.html: This is availability.
blocks.text: This is availability.

blocks.html: Now, all nodes are up, but, B is not able to communicate with A and C due to some network failure.
blocks.text: Now, all nodes are up, but, B is not able to communicate with A and C due to some network failure.

blocks.html: Node B can still handle requests from its clients.
blocks.text: Node B can still handle requests from its clients.

blocks.html: Nodes A and C continue serving their clients.
blocks.text: Nodes A and C continue serving their clients.

blocks.html: The system does not stop functioning, even though nodes cannot all talk to each other.
blocks.text: The system does not stop functioning, even though nodes cannot all talk to each other.

blocks.html: This is partition tolerance.
blocks.text: This is partition tolerance.

blocks.html: Availability vs Partition Tolerance
blocks.text: Availability vs Partition Tolerance

blocks.html: Availability: The system continues to work even when some nodes are down.
blocks.text: Availability: The system continues to work even when some nodes are down.

blocks.html: Partition Tolerance: The system continues to work when nodes lose communication among themselves.
blocks.text: Partition Tolerance: The system continues to work when nodes lose communication among themselves.

blocks.html: CAP Theorem
blocks.text: CAP Theorem

blocks.html: A distributed system can provide only two of the three: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance — never all three at the same time.
blocks.text: A distributed system can provide only two of the three: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance — never all three at the same time.

blocks.html: Why Choosing All (CAP) at Once Is Impossible?
blocks.text: Why Choosing All (CAP) at Once Is Impossible?

blocks.html: Example with 3 nodes A, B, and C storing variable X = 10.
blocks.text: Example with 3 nodes A, B, and C storing variable X = 10.

blocks.html: Client updates X = 20 at node A.
blocks.text: Client updates X = 20 at node A.

blocks.html: To keep Consistency, the update must also reach B and C.
blocks.text: To keep Consistency, the update must also reach B and C.

blocks.html: Now a partition occurs.
blocks.text: Now a partition occurs.

blocks.html: Node A is cut off from B and C.
blocks.text: Node A is cut off from B and C.

blocks.html: Clients still send requests to all nodes.
blocks.text: Clients still send requests to all nodes.

blocks.html: Trying to keep all three:
blocks.text: Trying to keep all three:

blocks.html: Consistency → All nodes must agree (X = 20 everywhere).
blocks.text: Consistency → All nodes must agree (X = 20 everywhere).

blocks.html: Availability → Each node must answer its clients.
blocks.text: Availability → Each node must answer its clients.

blocks.html: Partition Tolerance → Nodes must keep running despite the broken link.
blocks.text: Partition Tolerance → Nodes must keep running despite the broken link.

blocks.html: The contradiction:
blocks.text: The contradiction:

blocks.html: If A answers its client → A shows X = 20.
blocks.text: If A answers its client → A shows X = 20.

blocks.html: If B answers its client → B still has X = 10.
blocks.text: If B answers its client → B still has X = 10.

blocks.html: That breaks Consistency.
blocks.text: That breaks Consistency.

blocks.html: If A waits for B and C → clients at A get no response.
blocks.text: If A waits for B and C → clients at A get no response.

blocks.html: That breaks Availability.
blocks.text: That breaks Availability.

blocks.html: This explains that getting all three at once is impossible.
blocks.text: This explains that getting all three at once is impossible.

blocks.html: CA
blocks.text: CA

blocks.html: Choosing CA (Consistency + Availability) sounds tempting, but it is only possible when there are no network partitions. In real-world distributed systems, partitions are inevitable, which makes pure CA an unrealistic choice.
blocks.text: Choosing CA (Consistency + Availability) sounds tempting, but it is only possible when there are no network partitions. In real-world distributed systems, partitions are inevitable, which makes pure CA an unrealistic choice.

blocks.html: Example:
blocks.text: Example:

blocks.html: A single database server stores a variable X = 10.
blocks.text: A single database server stores a variable X = 10.

blocks.html: A client updates X = 20, and immediately every read reflects the new value.
blocks.text: A client updates X = 20, and immediately every read reflects the new value.

blocks.html: The system is consistent (all reads see the same value) and available (every request gets a response).
blocks.text: The system is consistent (all reads see the same value) and available (every request gets a response).

blocks.html: Now, imagine scaling this to 3 nodes: A, B, & C.
blocks.text: Now, imagine scaling this to 3 nodes: A, B, & C.

blocks.html: As long as the network is healthy, all nodes stay in sync → CA holds.
blocks.text: As long as the network is healthy, all nodes stay in sync → CA holds.

blocks.html: But if a network partition occurs (e.g., A is cut off from B and C):
blocks.text: But if a network partition occurs (e.g., A is cut off from B and C):

blocks.html: To remain consistent, either B and C must reject requests (sacrificing availability → CP),
blocks.text: To remain consistent, either B and C must reject requests (sacrificing availability → CP),

blocks.html: Or to remain available, B and C must continue serving possibly stale data (sacrificing consistency → AP).
blocks.text: Or to remain available, B and C must continue serving possibly stale data (sacrificing consistency → AP).

blocks.html: This shows that CA cannot be guaranteed once partitions happen.
blocks.text: This shows that CA cannot be guaranteed once partitions happen.

blocks.html: Key point:
blocks.text: Key point:

blocks.html: CA systems exist only in theory (with perfectly reliable networks) or in practice as single-node systems.
blocks.text: CA systems exist only in theory (with perfectly reliable networks) or in practice as single-node systems.

blocks.html: In distributed real-world systems, we always have to choose between CP and AP during partitions.
blocks.text: In distributed real-world systems, we always have to choose between CP and AP during partitions.

blocks.html: AP
blocks.text: AP

blocks.html: Choosing AP (Availability + Partition Tolerance) means the system always remains responsive, even during partitions, but consistency may be temporarily sacrificed.
blocks.text: Choosing AP (Availability + Partition Tolerance) means the system always remains responsive, even during partitions, but consistency may be temporarily sacrificed.

blocks.text: Example:

blocks.html: 3 Nodes: A, B, & C.
blocks.text: 3 Nodes: A, B, & C.

blocks.html: By default, clients near A talk to A and similarly for B and C.
blocks.text: By default, clients near A talk to A and similarly for B and C.

blocks.html: System stores a variable X = 10, means the variable is stored at each node.
blocks.text: System stores a variable X = 10, means the variable is stored at each node.

blocks.html: Client near A updates X = 20, means the value is updated at A.
blocks.text: Client near A updates X = 20, means the value is updated at A.

blocks.html: Now, a network partition occurs:
blocks.text: Now, a network partition occurs:

blocks.html: A is isolated from B and C.
blocks.text: A is isolated from B and C.

blocks.html: The changes are not propagated to B and C.
blocks.text: The changes are not propagated to B and C.

blocks.html: Clients of B and C can still access their local nodes.
blocks.text: Clients of B and C can still access their local nodes.

blocks.html: But they may still read X = 10, while clients near A read X = 20.
blocks.text: But they may still read X = 10, while clients near A read X = 20.

blocks.html: Consistency is lost, but the system continues serving all clients without downtime.
blocks.text: Consistency is lost, but the system continues serving all clients without downtime.

blocks.html: When to choose AP:
blocks.text: When to choose AP:

blocks.html: When availability is critical (e.g., social media feeds).
blocks.text: When availability is critical (e.g., social media feeds).

blocks.html: When temporary inconsistencies are acceptable and can be resolved later via eventual consistency.
blocks.text: When temporary inconsistencies are acceptable and can be resolved later via eventual consistency.

blocks.html: When user experience matters more than strict correctness in real time.
blocks.text: When user experience matters more than strict correctness in real time.

blocks.html: CP
blocks.text: CP

blocks.html: Choosing CP (Consistency + Partition Tolerance) means the system always ensures correctness across nodes, even during partitions, but availability may be sacrificed.
blocks.text: Choosing CP (Consistency + Partition Tolerance) means the system always ensures correctness across nodes, even during partitions, but availability may be sacrificed.
